entries.name: canvas-sketch
entries.use_for: Framework for making generative artwork in JS with export at print resolution
entries.why: Popular generative-art workflow with hot reload, exports and print-size output
entries.summary: canvas-sketch is a collection of tools and modules for creating generative art in JavaScript in the browser. Its CLI scaffolds and serves sketches, exports high-resolution PNGs at print dimensions (e.g. A4 at 300 DPI) with Cmd/Ctrl+S, supports templates such as Three.js, and can build sketches into a shareable HTML site.
entries.best_for: Generative artists making print-ready or high-resolution canvas artwork in JavaScript with a quick sketch-and-export workflow.
entries.not_for: Anyone wanting a GUI tool or a polished, fully documented framework; the roadmap lists API docs, GUI controls and tests as outstanding.

entries.name: css-doodle
entries.use_for: Generate patterns and visual art with CSS rules inside a web component.
entries.why: Unique CSS-driven approach to generative art; drop in a single element with no canvas code.
entries.summary: css-doodle is a web component for generative visual art written in CSS. You write CSS rules for a grid of cells, mixed with randomness and math functions, to draw patterns, backgrounds, icons and decorations; companion tools include a playground, an SVG playground and the cssd CLI for image/video export.
entries.best_for: Generating decorative patterns, backgrounds or generative art on web pages using CSS syntax with a single custom element.
entries.not_for: Pixel/shader-level graphics, 3D, or heavy interactive animation where canvas or WebGL tools are better suited.

entries.name: glslViewer
entries.use_for: Prototype and render GLSL shaders from the terminal with live reload.
entries.why: From the author of The Book of Shaders; renders 2D/3D shaders, exports frames and runs headless.
entries.summary: glslViewer is a console-based OpenGL sandbox that displays 2D and 3D GLSL fragment and vertex shaders without a UI. It hot-reloads files, loads textures, video, audio and models (PLY, OBJ, GLTF), accepts uniforms and commands via stdin or OSC, and can render headless and export images or PNG sequences.
entries.best_for: Live-coding and previewing GLSL shaders from the terminal or a script, including headless rendering and driving it via OSC or a Python wrapper.
entries.not_for: Users wanting a graphical shader editor or a high-level creative coding framework; it is built from source per platform.

entries.name: Hydra
entries.use_for: Live-code video synthesis and visuals in the browser for performances.
entries.why: Popular live-coding video synth with a chainable JS API that compiles to WebGL shaders; embeddable via hydra-synth.
entries.summary: Hydra is a browser-based environment for live-coding visuals, inspired by analog modular synthesizers. It chains coordinate and color transform functions over multiple framebuffers and can stream and mix video between connected browsers; the synth engine is also available as the hydra-synth npm module.
entries.best_for: Live visuals performances, VJ-style sketches and networked collaborative visuals coded in the browser.
entries.not_for: Production apps or broad browser support; the README says it is experimental and only works on Chrome/Chromium with WebGL.

entries.name: nannou
entries.use_for: Creative coding framework for Rust: graphics, audio, lasers and more
entries.why: The main Rust creative coding framework, inspired by Processing and openFrameworks

license_verified.note: Crates are MIT OR Apache-2.0 per workspace Cargo.toml; license files live in crate folders

entries.summary: nannou is an open-source creative-coding toolkit for Rust, inspired by Processing, openFrameworks and Cinder. It is built on the Bevy game engine and exposes its sketch/app API and Draw interface as Bevy plugins, with examples including ports of Generative Design and Nature of Code.
entries.best_for: Artists and developers who want to write creative-coding sketches or installations in Rust, or add a Processing-style draw API to a Bevy app.
entries.not_for: Beginners wanting a browser-based or non-Rust tool; the README says it is still early days, and first builds can be slow.

entries.name: openFrameworks
entries.use_for: Build high-performance interactive installations and visuals in C++.
entries.why: Long-running C++ toolkit for artists with addons for OpenCV, audio, Kinect and more; MIT licensed (verified).
entries.summary: openFrameworks is a C++ toolkit for creative coding. It ships as a folder of core libraries, addons, examples and an apps directory for your projects, and builds on Windows, Linux (including ARM), macOS and Emscripten.
entries.best_for: Creative coders building native, performance-sensitive interactive art or installations in C++ across desktop platforms.
entries.not_for: Those who want a scripting or browser-first workflow; it requires C++ and per-platform setup (nightly releases avoid submodule cloning).

entries.name: p5.js
entries.use_for: Sketch interactive graphics, generative art and visual experiments in the browser.
entries.why: The best-known creative-coding library for the web, with a huge community, examples and an online editor.
entries.summary: p5.js is a free, open-source JavaScript library for accessible creative coding in the browser, using setup() and draw() sketch functions. It provides drawing tools and supports audio-visual, interactive and generative work, with a web editor, extensive documentation and community libraries.
entries.best_for: Beginners, artists, designers and educators making interactive or generative sketches for the web with a Processing-style API.
entries.not_for: Native or high-performance desktop graphics, or large production web apps; the project also does not accept fully AI-generated contributions.

entries.name: Paper Shaders
entries.use_for: Drop ready-made animated shader effects (gradients, noise, patterns) into a web page.
entries.why: Zero-dependency canvas shaders installable from npm, with React components and tunable parameters.
entries.summary: Zero-dependency HTML canvas shaders published as a vanilla package and a React package (@paper-design/shaders-react), with components such as MeshGradient and DotOrbit. Shaders can be animated or static and are configured through props like colors, distortion, swirl and speed; they can also be designed visually in Paper and exported as code.
entries.best_for: Adding lightweight animated shader textures, gradients or masked backgrounds to a website or React app without pulling in a 3D engine.
entries.not_for: Still on 0.0.x versioning with breaking changes expected, so dependencies must be pinned. A set of ready-made background effects, not a general WebGL or 3D rendering framework.

entries.name: Pts
entries.use_for: Create generative and interactive visualizations with geometry primitives on canvas.
entries.why: Lightweight TypeScript library that treats points and forms as composable primitives; clean API for sketching.
entries.summary: Pts is a TypeScript and JavaScript library for visualization and creative coding, built around primitives like Pt, Group, Line and CanvasSpace. It ships as an ESM-first npm package with a CommonJS entry, or as a browser script exposing globalThis.Pts, with starter kits and React integrations.
entries.best_for: Creative coding, generative art and interactive canvas visualizations in JS/TS where you want geometric primitives and a drawing space abstraction.
entries.not_for: Not a charting or dashboard library; you build visuals from points and shapes yourself. Canvas-oriented, not a 3D or game engine.

entries.name: Samila
entries.use_for: Generate reproducible generative-art images from Python.
entries.why: Simple Python generator built on matplotlib; seeds make pieces reproducible and easy to export.
entries.summary: Python generative art generator. Each image plots many thousand points whose positions come from two user-supplied (or random) functions with random parameters, then projects them (e.g. polar) with matplotlib. A seed makes results reproducible.
entries.best_for: Making reproducible generative art images from Python scripts, quick experiments with function-based point plots, exporting images or configs.
entries.not_for: Interactive or real-time visuals, 3D, shader work, or JS/browser art. Output is static matplotlib point plots only.

entries.name: thi.ng/umbrella
entries.use_for: Monorepo of 200+ TypeScript packages for geometry, color, generative art and data
entries.why: Huge, well-documented toolkit for computational design and generative art in TS
entries.summary: Monorepo of 200+ TypeScript packages for computational design: geometry, color, vectors/matrices, random numbers, reactive streams, WebGL/GPGPU, DSLs, data structures and file formats. Designed as composable functional libraries rather than a framework. Development has moved to Codeberg; GitHub is a read-only mirror.
entries.best_for: Generative art and creative coding in TypeScript where you want to pick individual composable packages (geometry, color, streams, WebGL).
entries.not_for: Developers wanting one batteries-included framework or a gentle learning curve. Huge surface area; the GitHub repo is a mirror, active work is on Codeberg.

entries.name: VFX-JS
entries.use_for: Apply WebGL shader effects to images, videos and text on a web page.
entries.why: Small library that overlays GLSL effects on DOM elements with a few lines of code.
entries.summary: JavaScript library that applies WebGL shader effects to DOM elements such as images, videos and text. You call vfx.add(element, {shader}) with a built-in shader name or compose prebuilt effects from @vfx-js/effects (bloom, pixelate); React bindings are in @vfx-js/react.
entries.best_for: Adding glitch, bloom, pixelate or custom GLSL effects to images, video or text on a regular web page with a few lines of code.
entries.not_for: Full 3D scenes or game rendering (use three.js), or non-web targets. It is a DOM-overlay effects layer only.
